newsitem.title: USA: SoCal Edison non-generation incentives set.
newsitem.headline: SoCal Edison non-generation incentives set.

text.p: Edison International's Southern California Edison Co. received approval Friday from the Calfornia Public Utilities Commission (CPUC) to institute performance-based ratemaking for non-generation costs, such as transmission and distribution operations, as of January 1997.
Under this system, called PBR, utilities have an incentive to boost efficiency and cut costs since any savings will be shared by shareholders and customers.
Under traditional general rate cases, utilities are allocated a fixed return on operating costs.

Edison chairman and chief executive officer John Bryson said "PBR provides the utility with greater long-term incentives for lower rates, increases management flexibility and accountabiilty, rewards utilities for providing increased customer value, and reduces the cost and complexity of regulatory proceedings."
Under its 1995 general rate case, Edison's transmission and distribution revenue requirement is about $2.1 billion of its $7.3 billion total requirement, the company said.
A net revenue sharing mechanism in the PBR system determines how customers and shareholders will share gains and losses from transmission and distribution operations.
Edison requested a PBR that would include customer growth based on forecasts, but the CPUC said it declined to include this factor because forecasting would require more regulatory intervention.
Edison's authorized rate of return on equity will be adjusted based on changes in interest rates for AA utility bonds.
Beginning in 1998, the transmission portion will be separated from the non-generation revenue requirement and subject to ratemaking under the rules of the Federal Energy Regulatory Commission.
